title: Cheapest Route
statement: A courier network has `n` hubs numbered `1` to `n` and `m` one-way roads. Each road has a toll. Find the cheapest total toll for travelling from hub `s` to hub `t`.

Roads are directed: a road `u v w` can only be used from `u` to `v`. There may be several roads between the same pair of hubs, roads from a hub to itself, and roads with toll `0`. Travelling from a hub to itself costs `0`.
inputFormat: The first line contains four integers `n m s t`.
Each of the next `m` lines contains three integers `u v w`: a road from `u` to `v` with toll `w`.
outputFormat: Print the minimum total toll from `s` to `t`, or `-1` if `t` cannot be reached.
constraints: A route cost can reach about 10^14. Use a 64-bit integer type (long in Java/C#, long long in C++).

examples.explanation: Two cheap roads beat the direct road.

input: Next m lines: u v w (directed road u -> v with toll w)
starter.output: the minimum total toll from s to t, or -1 (may need 64-bit)

private.complexity: O((n + m) log n) Dijkstra with a binary heap and lazy deletion. Bellman-Ford O(n·m) times out.
private.notes: Skip heap entries whose distance is larger than the best known distance. Zero-weight edges are fine for Dijkstra.
